page.layout: One page of text, set as verse in four-line stanzas, with the lines at the top and running head above; a catchword at the lower right.

p.i: Testes saepe tuis aequoribus rates Fracta, puniceo sanguine decolor Pontus, Luctificis oppida subruta Flammis, captaque moenia.
Nonne obsessa vides littora milite Anglo cuncta, simul nautibus obrutos Fluctus innumeris, vela minantia, Telorum strepitus graves,
Ignemque Aeolio sulphure feruidum, Clades ferre tuis puppibus asperas Doctum? Nonne vides impavidas Ducum Mentes, exitium tuae
Gentis? Cerne piam pectore prouido Reginam, procerum consiliis sacris Erectam, ut trepidas strenua patriae Duris rebus opem ferat.
Sic qui puppe sedens celsior imperat Nautarum pavidas sedulus excitat Mentes, Si scopulos cautus & Africi Vitat praecipites minas:
Castigatque moras, quum maris impiger Irati tumidos murmura tollere Fluctus, seque diem condere percipit Nimbis tristibus obrutum.
Sic pastor vigiles follicitat canum Prudens excubias, quum gregibus timet Infirmis, amidos [?] quum trepidantibus Propellit stabulis lupos.

page.notes: Stanza breaks are inferred from the four-line grouping of the verse; the lines are set without indentation. "amidos" (line 27) is doubtful, possibly "amicos". "Heu," at the lower right is a catchword, set apart from the text. The running head is printed with its comma.
